Settings of the optimizer used by fit()

Source: R/finn-control.R
finnControl.Rd

Collects the settings of the optimization behind fit() in one object, passed as fit(control = finnControl(...)). The defaults are robust in most cases: a fit needs no control argument at all. The learning rate lr, the number of epochs and the batchsize are changed much more often, so they stay arguments of fit() itself.

Usage

finnControl(
  optimizer = torch::optim_ignite_adam,
  lr_scheduler = "none",
  lr_scheduler_params = list(),
  clip_norm = 2,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'finnControl'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

optimizer

(function)
A torch optimizer generator. Default torch::optim_ignite_adam.

lr_scheduler

(character(1) or function)
Learning-rate schedule: "none" (default), "step", "exponential", "cosine", "plateau", or a function(optimizer) returning a torch scheduler. See Details.

lr_scheduler_params

(list)
Settings of the chosen schedule. See Details.

clip_norm

(numeric(1) or named list)
Gradient-norm budget per parameter group. Default 2.

...

Further arguments for optimizer, e.g. weight_decay = 1e-4.

x

(finnControl)
The object to print.

Value

A list of class finnControl, to be passed to fit(control = ).

Details

fit() estimates the parameters by gradient descent: in every epoch it simulates the sites, compares the simulation with the observations (see finn_loss), and moves every parameter a small step in the direction that makes the comparison better. finnControl() sets how those steps are taken.

  • optimizer is the rule that turns a gradient into a step. The default, Adam (torch::optim_ignite_adam), adapts the step size per parameter and works well without tuning. Any torch optimizer generator can be passed; extra arguments for it, such as weight_decay, go into ....

  • lr_scheduler lowers the learning rate during the fit. The default "none" keeps lr constant. "step" multiplies the learning rate by gamma every step_size epochs, "exponential" multiplies it by gamma every epoch, "cosine" lets it fall smoothly to eta_min over T_max epochs, and "plateau" lowers it by factor after patience epochs without an improvement of the total loss. A schedule helps when the losses keep oscillating late in a fit. Advanced: a function(optimizer) that returns a torch learning-rate scheduler (an object with a $step() method).

  • lr_scheduler_params tunes the chosen schedule, e.g. list(step_size = 50, gamma = 0.5) for "step", list(T_max = 200) for "cosine", list(factor = 0.5, patience = 20) for "plateau". Entries that are not given take defaults scaled to epochs and lr.

  • clip_norm limits how large a single step can be. Gradients are clipped to this norm, separately for three groups of parameters (the species parameters of the mechanistic processes, the environmental-response networks, and the parameters of the likelihoods), so that a group with large gradients cannot swamp the others. A single number applies the same budget to every group; a named list, e.g. list(mechanistic = 2, nn = 1, loss = 5), sets groups individually.

Before 0.2.0 these were arguments of fit() itself. The old form is still accepted with a warning, e.g. fit(lr_scheduler = "step") becomes fit(control = finnControl(lr_scheduler = "step")).

See also

fit(), finn_loss

Examples

# the defaults, which most fits can keep
finnControl()
#> FINN optimizer settings (fit(control = ))
#>   optimizer:            Adam (torch::optim_ignite_adam) 
#>   lr_scheduler:         none 
#>   clip_norm:            2 

# halve the learning rate every 50 epochs and allow larger steps
ctrl <- finnControl(lr_scheduler = "step",
                    lr_scheduler_params = list(step_size = 50, gamma = 0.5),
                    clip_norm = 5)

library(data.table)
sites <- 1:3
Nsp   <- max(fia_obs_dt$species)
init  <- makeInitCohorts(fia_init_trees[siteID %in% sites], Nspecies = Nsp)
m <- finn(N_species = Nsp, recruits_dbh = 12.9,
          growth_process       = createProcess(~ temp + prec, growth),
          mortality_process    = createProcess(~ temp + prec, mortality),
          regeneration_process = createProcess(~ temp + prec, regeneration_capped))
fit(m, data = fia_obs_dt[siteID %in% sites], env = fia_env_dt[siteID %in% sites],
    init_cohort = init, epochs = 2L, patches = 4, patch_size = 0.06,
    control = ctrl, plot_progress = FALSE)
#> ℹ weights: intercept-only baseline x your vector (dbh=0.00243, ba=12, trees=0.968, growth=1.84e+04, mortality=38.5, regeneration=0.768)
#> ℹ share of the objective at the intercept-only baseline (scaled): dbh=17%, ba=17%, trees=17%, growth=17%, mortality=17%, regeneration=17%
